description_in_figure: Full-length color diagram of adult C. elegans hermaphrodite, ventral view, nose to left, tail to right. Labeled structures: pharynx, pharyngeal-intestinal valve, intestine, gonad arm, spermatheca, vulva, fertilized egg, stomatointestinal muscle, anus.
ai_summary: One of three panels in IntFIG1 depicting the intestine. This panel is a labeled diagram, a graphic rendition based on Wood et al. 1996, showing the intestine's position within the whole worm from a ventral view. The intestine runs along the left side of the body anterior to the vulva and switches to the right side posterior to it. Surrounding structures shown include the pharynx and pharyngeal-intestinal valve at the anterior end, the gonad arm, spermatheca, vulva, and a fertilized egg near the midbody, and the stomatointestinal muscle and anus at the posterior end. This overview diagram establishes the intestine's overall anatomical context relative to the reproductive and digestive systems before the following panels show it in live tissue.

description_in_figure: Full-length DIC image of the same anatomical region, ventral view, nose to left, tail to right. Visible structures: pharynx, intestine, distal gonad, proximal gonad, fertilized eggs, vulva, intestinal turn, and a second distal gonad arm.
ai_summary: One of three panels in IntFIG1 depicting the intestine. This is a DIC (Differential Interference Contrast) micrograph at 400x magnification showing the adult intestine running parallel to the gonad along the length of the body, ventral view. The image captures the intestine alongside the pharynx anteriorly, the proximal and distal gonad arms, fertilized eggs mid-body, the vulva, and a visible turn in the intestine partway along its length. Unlike the labeled schematic in panel A, this panel shows the real tissue relationships as seen under live imaging, illustrating how closely the intestine and reproductive tract run alongside one another in the adult hermaphrodite.

description_in_figure: Same animal as panel B. Epifluorescent image focused on the intestine, showing autofluorescent birefringent gut granules filling the intestine along most of its length.
ai_summary: One of three panels in IntFIG1 depicting the intestine. This epifluorescent image, taken of the same animal shown in panel B at 400x magnification, reveals autofluorescent birefringent gut granules densely filling the intestine throughout nearly its entire length. These granules are a natural, unstained autofluorescent feature of intestinal cells and are commonly used as a visual marker to confirm intestinal identity and integrity under fluorescence imaging. This panel demonstrates a key distinguishing visual feature of the C. elegans intestine that is not visible under standard DIC imaging.
